html_en:
A day of quiet intensity in the AI world: a major launch pressed early, a retinal chip restoring sight in Europe, and a growing chorus of builders asking whether the AI product explosion is producing anything meaningfully new.

🚀 Something Big Just Shipped (Early)

The most intriguing story of the day came in fragments. @thsottiaux — whose identity and affiliation remain deliberately vague in the feed — dropped a series of cryptic, high-engagement tweets that read like a product launch in slow motion.

"Team is cooking like never before." — @thsottiaux

Then, in quick succession: a landing time ("2:30pm PST"), followed by the reveal that whatever was planned had already shipped ahead of schedule:

"This celebration is moved to tomorrow as the button was already pressed today." — @thsottiaux

Nearly 7,000 likes on that last one — remarkable engagement for an announcement that reveals almost nothing. Whatever dropped, the builder community is watching closely.

🛠️ The Unglamorous Craft of CLI Agents

While mystery launches grabbed attention, Guillermo Rauch was doing the quieter work of shipping a real tool. Version 0.0.7 of fx — his CLI agent — landed with meaningfully improved MCP support and a more minimal tool surface. The integrations list reads like a who's who of the developer stack: @context7ai, @datadoghq, @supabase, @notionhq, @linear, and more.

But the most honest note in his announcement was about the unsexy problem that trips up nearly every agent builder:

"One of the trickiest things about CLI agents is that running commands is actually not that simple. Commands might hang or run for very long, their output needs to be monitorable by the agent, they might produce huge amounts of output, or none." — @rauchg

Meanwhile, @petergyang captured the surreal texture of this agentic moment from the user's side: "It's a really weird feeling entering 2FA into a cloud computer." The gap between "agent does tasks for you" and "agent is you, to the system" remains philosophically unresolved — and increasingly practical.

🧠 Restoring Sight, Reimagining the Brain

The day's most substantive long-form content came from No Priors, whose conversation with Max Hodak — founder of Science Corp and formerly of Neuralink — covered the moment a retinal prosthesis chip became commercially available in Europe. Watch/Listen: No Priors: From Restoring Sight to Reimagining the Brain, with Max Hodak

Hodak's framing of the brain is arrestingly direct:

"The brain very literally, very clearly, plainly is a computer. We talk about being a brain in a vat. That's what the skull is. Like the brain is connected to the environment through a small number of wires, the cranial and spinal nerves, these little cables that carry your interaction with the world." — Max Hodak

Science's Prima implant — a tiny chip placed under the retina, paired with laser-projecting glasses — just received CE marketing approval in Europe, with first commercial sales imminent. Hodak is clear-eyed about why this matters beyond the technology itself:

"People forget that the moonshot worked. Like, we left boot prints on the moon. It has gotten used in Silicon Valley to mean these things that have extremely long odds and are unlikely to work, and therefore we can vaporize a bunch of investor money just fine." — Max Hodak

The company is also developing a separate gene therapy track expected to enter human trials next year. The vision (literal and strategic) is compounding: better grayscale first, then color channels, then richer signal fidelity — engineering as a patient accumulation of gains.

😵 The AI Product Blur — and the RSI Horizon

Two very different observers landed on a shared anxiety today: the AI ecosystem is simultaneously accelerating and homogenizing.

@zarazhangrui put it with the bluntness of someone who has clearly downloaded too many apps this week:

"Never had so many AI products looked so similar. Every time I open this app it feels like homework: yet another new product to learn that promises to do the same thing but somehow better; the specific ways in which it's better isn't clear unless you invest hours actually trying it." — @zarazhangrui

There's a structural reason for the blur: every product asks for the same permissions (Gmail, Notion, GitHub, Slack, Calendar), wraps a similar model, and differentiates on vibes. The UX debt is piling up faster than the underlying capability is differentiating.

Zooming out further, Matt Turck flagged a prediction worth sitting with. Citing @RyanGreenblatt, he noted:

"All frontier AI labs are basically working on the same thing: recursive self improvement (RSI), meaning AI building AI. This could lead to an AI takeover as early as late 2028 or 2029." — @mattturck

@thenanyu had perhaps the most economical response to all of this: "we're gonna need mentats aren't we." The Dune reference lands differently when you're entering 2FA on behalf of an agent.

💬 On Culture: Building vs. Dunking

A quieter thread worth noting: @nikunj posted a thoughtful pushback against the dunking reflex that tends to spike whenever a high-profile AI launch stumbles or a competitor makes news.

"It's the perfect dopamine loop — other people join in and you feel great. But it just screams envy and doesn't lead to anything productive. If you think you can do it better, go do that then. Keep building. Continue to change the world. That's the best way to have impact." — @nikunj

Good advice for any day, but especially on one where a major model lab price war appears to be quietly escalating. Nikunj separately flagged that subsidized token prices from competing labs are likely to drift upward as compute shortages bite — "say goodbye to your reset limits" — which will filter out the most casual experimenters and concentrate serious usage. The competitive reset may be coming sooner than the current pricing landscape suggests.
html_zh:
一个神秘的发布倒计时、AI产品同质化的焦虑，以及让盲人重见光明的芯片——今天的科技圈，戏剧性与真实突破并存。

🚀 有什么大事要来了？

今天推特上最引人注目的悬念来自 @thsottiaux。他接连发出三条神秘推文，却没有透露任何细节：

"团队正在以前所未有的状态全力冲刺。" — @thsottiaux
"庆祝活动推迟到明天，因为按钮今天已经按下了。" — @thsottiaux

"按钮已经按下"这句话获得了近七千个点赞——在AI圈，这种神秘的预告往往意味着一次重要发布。我们拭目以待。

🤖 CLI代理的细节魔鬼

Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 发布了他的命令行AI工具 fx 0.0.7，并罕见地坦诚谈到了构建CLI代理的真实难点：

"关于CLI代理，最棘手的事情之一是：运行命令其实并不简单。命令可能会卡住或运行很长时间，其输出需要被代理实时监控，它们可能产生海量输出，也可能什么都不输出。这正是 fx 真正出彩的地方，并且会持续改进。" — @rauchg

此次更新大幅改进了MCP支持，集成了 Context7、Datadog、MongoDB、Linear、Notion、Supabase 等主流工具。工具数量更少、shell执行更精准——这是一种克制的产品哲学，在当前"功能堆砌"的AI工具浪潮中显得格外清醒。

😩 AI产品同质化：一场审美疲劳

最直击灵魂的吐槽来自 @zarazhangrui，她精准描述了许多人对当下AI产品爆炸的真实感受：

"从来没有这么多AI产品看起来如此相似。即使产品数量在爆炸式增长，真正激进的新想法却寥寥无几，一切都模糊成一团。每次打开某个新应用，感觉像是在做作业：又一个新产品要学，它声称做同样的事但不知怎么更好——而它具体好在哪里，除非你花几个小时认真试用，根本看不出来。" — @zarazhangrui

她还补刀：每个产品都要求接入 Gmail、Calendar、Notion、Granola、GitHub、Slack……这种"权限索取竞赛"本身就是一种疲惫。这番话，恐怕说出了很多普通用户的心声。

与此同时，@nikunj 从投资人视角观察到另一个趋势：大模型厂商之间的价格战正在升温，但补贴不会永远持续：

"大型模型实验室正在开战——这是必然的。看着吧，不到六个月，随着算力成本和短缺开始被'真实感受到'，补贴后的Token价格会上涨。和你的重置限额说再见吧。" — @nikunj

🧠 让盲人重见光明：比任何AI演示都更震撼的真实突破

今天最值得深读的内容，来自播客 No Priors 对 Max Hodak（Science公司创始人、前Neuralink联合创始人）的专访。他的公司刚刚在欧洲获得 Prima 视网膜假体的商业销售许可——这是一块植入眼球视网膜下方的微型芯片，配合激光投影眼镜，可以绕过已死亡的视杆和视锥细胞，直接刺激视网膜，让失明患者重获视觉信号。

Watch/Listen: No Priors — From Restoring Sight to Reimagining the Brain, with Max Hodak
"大脑，从字面意义上说，就是一台计算机。你可以通过以特定方式排列物质来解决计算问题，然后放手，按下启动键。我们谈论'缸中之脑'——颅骨就是那个缸。大脑通过少数几根'电线'与外界相连，那就是颅神经和脊髓神经，这些细小的线缆承载着你与世界的所有互动。" — Max Hodak

他还对"登月项目"这一说法做出了精彩的重新定义：

"人们忘记了，登月任务成功了。我们真的在月球上留下了脚印。在硅谷，'登月'这个词已经被滥用，变成了'极低概率、大概率失败、所以烧掉一堆投资人的钱也没关系'的代名词。但历史上，登月任务的成功率比人们认为的要高得多。最重要的事情之一，是在这里建立一个真实的业务——而这，就是起点。" — Max Hodak

在AI圈日复一日的基准测试竞争与产品发布轰炸之外，这个真实地让人重见光明的故事，提醒我们：技术的终极意义，始终是人。

💬 今日杂谈

@petergyang 分享了一个颇具时代感的感受：

"说实话，在云端电脑里输入双重验证码，感觉真的很奇怪。" — @petergyang

而 Matt Turck 则转发了一个更宏观的判断：所有前沿AI实验室本质上都在做同一件事——递归自我改进（RSI），即AI构建AI。研究员 Ryan Greenblatt 认为，这可能最早在2028至2029年导致AI接管的临界点。这个话题，或许比任何产品发布都更值得认真对待。
